title: "Chapter Template & Formatting Reference"
---

This page is a **reference, not a real chapter**. These are snipetts I use to reference quarto and tex syntax. It reads as notes-to-self.

To start a new chapter:

1. Copy `template.qmd` → `chapterNN.qmd`.
2. Replace the YAML `title`.
3. Add the page to the sidebar in `_quarto.yml` under `Solutions`.
4. Keep one `##` heading per problem so the right-hand table of contents
   tracks your progress.

---

## Problem 1 — inline & display math {#sec-tmpl-1}

Inline math goes between single dollar signs: the estimator $\hat\theta_n$ is
unbiased when $\mathbb{E}[\hat\theta_n] = \theta$.

Display math (centered, its own line) goes between double dollar signs:

$$
\mathbb{P}(A \cup B) = \mathbb{P}(A) + \mathbb{P}(B) - \mathbb{P}(A \cap B).
$$

A numbered, referenceable equation uses an `{#eq-...}` label:

$$
\bar X_n = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} X_i
$$ {#eq-mean}

…which you can cite later as @eq-mean.

## Problem 2 — multi-line aligned derivations {#sec-tmpl-2}

Use an `aligned` environment for step-by-step algebra. The `&` marks the
alignment column; `\\` ends a line.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}(X)
  &= \mathbb{E}\big[(X - \mu)^2\big] \\
  &= \mathbb{E}[X^2] - 2\mu\,\mathbb{E}[X] + \mu^2 \\
  &= \mathbb{E}[X^2] - \mu^2.
\end{aligned}
$$

Common symbols cheat-sheet: $\sum, \prod, \int, \infty, \partial,
\sim, \propto, \approx, \leq, \geq, \neq, \in, \subset, \cup, \cap,
\mid, \forall, \exists$; Greek $\alpha,\beta,\theta,\mu,\sigma,\lambda$;
blackboard $\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{E}, \mathbb{P}, \mathbb{N}$; hats/bars
$\hat\theta, \bar X, \tilde p$; distributions $X \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)$.

## Problem 3 — writing a proof {#sec-tmpl-3}

State what you're proving, then give the argument. The `{.proof}` callout is a
clean way to set it off (the QED box is added automatically by the closing).

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## Claim
If $A \subseteq B$ then $\mathbb{P}(A) \le \mathbb{P}(B)$.
:::

::: {.proof}
Write $B = A \cup (B \setminus A)$, a disjoint union. By additivity,
$$
\mathbb{P}(B) = \mathbb{P}(A) + \mathbb{P}(B \setminus A).
$$
Since $\mathbb{P}(B \setminus A) \ge 0$, we conclude $\mathbb{P}(B) \ge
\mathbb{P}(A)$. $\blacksquare$
:::

You can also do a quick informal proof inline with a final $\square$ or
$\blacksquare$ to mark the end.

## Problem 4 — code (Python / R) {#sec-tmpl-4}

Code blocks are syntax-highlighted. By default they are **shown but not run**
(see `execute:` in `_quarto.yml`). This is fine for illustrating an approach.

```python
import numpy as np

# Monte Carlo estimate of P(X + Y > 1) for X, Y ~ Uniform(0,1)
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
n = 1_000_000
x, y = rng.random(n), rng.random(n)
print((x + y > 1).mean())   # ≈ 0.5
```

```r
# Same idea in R
set.seed(0)
n <- 1e6
x <- runif(n); y <- runif(n)
mean(x + y > 1)   # ~0.5
```

To actually **execute** a chunk at render time and show its output, add the
engine + label and turn execution on for that block (requires the kernel
installed locally), e.g.:

```{{python}}
#| echo: true
1 + 1
```

(Double braces above are just so this template displays the syntax literally;
in a real chapter use single braces: `{python}`.)
